events.title: Meet N-zo: The AI Assistant that understands your business
events.description:
Artificial intelligence is entering a new phase: no longer limited to content generation or informational support, but gaining the ability to truly understand complex IT environments, analyze real-time operational data, and enable faster, safer, and more informed actions.
In this session, Matteo Brusco, Distribution Sales Manager Southern Europe at N-able, will present N-able’s vision for AI applied to IT management, cybersecurity, and operational automation, with a focus on N-zo, the AI assistant integrated into the N-able ecosystem.
N-zo is designed to support technicians, MSPs, IT teams, and security teams in the daily management of increasingly distributed infrastructures: from device status summarization to troubleshooting, from vulnerability analysis to intelligent documentation search, and toward future scenarios of agentic automation. The goal is simple yet strategic: reduce time spent on repetitive tasks, improve decision quality, and strengthen business operational resilience.
Through concrete use cases, customer feedback, and an evolving roadmap focused on AI assistants, expert agents, predictive automation, and cross-platform workflows, the session will show how N-able is transforming AI into a true ally for efficiency, security, and business continuity. The presentation highlights measurable benefits, including an average time saving of around 70% and operational speed improvements of 2–5x in common documentation and troubleshooting tasks.

events.title: From Hype to Impact: how Save the Children Is Applying AI in the Nonprofit Sector
events.description: How do you move from experimentation to the concrete adoption of AI in a large nonprofit organization? In this session, Save the Children will share several real-world use cases that have already been implemented, both in programs serving beneficiaries and in internal operations. It will be a pragmatic discussion on opportunities, limitations, governance, and lessons learned—designed for anyone looking to understand how to truly introduce artificial intelligence into the nonprofit sector without stopping at theory.

events.title: Building Agentic AI solutions with AWS: tools, best practices, and use cases
events.description: Agentic AI is redefining how companies design processes, services, and decision-making by introducing systems capable of understanding context, acting autonomously, and collaborating with people and applications. This talk will provide an overview of AWS solutions for designing and governing agentic AI architectures, exploring tools such as Amazon Bedrock, AgentCore, and Strands, along with patterns and best practices for production adoption. It will cover topics such as scalability, security, integration, and real-world use cases, to understand how to turn innovation into a real competitive advantage.

events.title: Customers are asking AI who to buy from. And the answer is not you. The GEO protocol to dominate AI responses
events.description:
While you’re reading these lines, your customers are delegating their purchasing decisions to AI systems like ChatGPT, Gemini, and Claude. And the AI is recommending your competitors.
Everything you’ve built on Google and social media risks becoming invisible. Ignoring optimization for the new AI-driven search engines means condemning your brand to total irrelevance—wasting all the investments you’ve made so far.
Ale Agostini (CEO of AvantGrade.com and author of Being the Answer) strips away any illusion and delivers the hard truth about GEO AI Search—the new paradigm of search in the age of artificial intelligence.
This is a practical session that overturns the status quo and shows you how to make AI cite your company as an authoritative source. By the end, you’ll feel one urgent need: to understand how much your business is losing—and take action fast.
What you’ll take away:
The invisibility diagnosis: why new AI search engines ignore your brand—and how to reverse the damage to your revenue.
The power shift: a strategic roadmap to leverage everything you’ve already built on Google and start appearing in the answers AI shows your potential customers.
The verdict (immediate action): a method to ensure maximum accuracy and presence of your brand identity in AI, through real-time testing of your “Brand AI integrity.”

events.title: Ban it or teach it? The AI dilemma in schools, seen by Digital 4 Children
events.description:
The debate around artificial intelligence in schools often swings between two extremes: strict bans or open access without guidance. Meanwhile, students are already using it daily, outside any educational framework.

In this context, the experience of Digital 4 Children comes into play, bringing digital education programs directly into schools. The focus thus shifts from control to education, from access to AI to how younger generations learn to use it.

events.title: Artist’s Confession in the Age of AI
The real breakthrough in AI isn’t speed. It’s shared understandin
events.description:
Everyone is racing to make AI faster, cheaper, and bigger. But when the model speaks, does anyone actually understand?
In this session, Oddmund and Sven will unpack three gaps hiding in plain sight across the AI landscape and explain why the industry is obsessed with the first one while barely talking about the other two. 
 They'll introduce the Comprehension Layer: the unsolved space between what AI produces and what humans actually need to understand, across languages, cultures, and high-stakes live environments.
 Drawing on Interprefy's experience powering real-time multilingual communication at scale — long before AI made it fashionable — this talk will challenge how the room thinks about what winning in AI actually looks like. Expect a frank conversation about infrastructure over hype, clarity over noise, and why the companies still standing in three years won't be the ones who shouted loudest. They'll be the ones who were most understood.

Ester Anzalone (Director of Digital Transformation, Metropolitan City of Milan) illustrates how an organization serving 133 municipalities and 3.2 million citizens deployed an AI agent to support citizens 24/7, reduce response times, and free operators from repetitive requests—while ensuring full compliance with AgID guidelines and ACN regulations.

events.title: The Innovative Travels of Gulliver – When Apps Learn to Walk

We will explore two topics that are redefining the boundaries of software development: AI Physics, the shift from intelligence that analyzes data to intelligence that operates according to the laws of physics, and the Humanoid as a Platform, a logical choice for integrating robotics into a world designed for humans, without disrupting existing infrastructures.

events.title: Your Brain on ChatGPT
events.description:
Join Dr. Nataliya Kosmyna of the MIT Media Lab for a discussion on the use of AI and its effects on the human brain.
For millions of years, human intelligence set the standard. But now, the lightning pace of tech has left us gasping, struggling to keep up with our own cognitive demands. AI has pushed civilization into overdrive, yet what we are ultimately doing is burning terawatts of power on data centers and excluding humans from this growth. We have built systems that are prefixed ‘smart’, but not smart enough to break free from their own inefficiency. Technology should amplify our creativity, not snuff it out. It should fuel social interactions, not isolate us. Instead, we are trapped in a dystopian remix of 1984 - 2026’s version - where digital censorship and surveillance threaten to choke innovation in nations that refuse to play along. This talk will explore critical questions: What should define ownership in the age of AI and at what cost?
Dr. Kosmyna is a research scientist at MIT Media Lab’s Fluid Interfaces group and a Visiting Research Faculty at Google. She has over 16 years of experience in developing and designing end-to-end brain-computer interfaces (BCIs). Coming from a background in artificial intelligence, neuroscience, and human computer interaction, she is passionate about the idea of creating a partnership between AI and human intelligence, a fusion of the machine with the human brain.

But the real turning point comes when AI stops being a brilliant demo or a set of isolated use cases and becomes a widespread organizational capability: governed, integrated, secure, and tangible. In this dual presentation, Cluster Reply and Unipol will explain what it means to make this transition: building the foundations so that GenAI does not remain a promise, but becomes a real engine of evolution for people, processes, and business. From platform design to guardrails, from reusable assets to use cases embedded in daily operations, a clear vision will emerge: the value of AI does not come only from the power of models, but from the ability to deploy them with responsibility, method, and courage. An inspiring story on how AI is brought from the lab to the heart of the enterprise.

events.title: SaaSpocalypse: everyone is talking about it. Few have understood it

The SaaSpocalypse is not a technological crisis. It is a crisis of understanding. For decades, companies have accumulated software as if quantity would produce intelligence. But it has produced complexity. The paradox is brutal: the more AI you introduce into a chaotic architecture, the more chaos you create. The power of models is already a commodity. The ability to execute is not.
The real question is not how much or which AI you are adopting. It is whether your organization is ready to govern it as it scales and to continuously transform itself.

events.title: Who killed AI? How we moved from automation to superpowers — and what we learned along the way.
events.description:
Almost two human years invested in AI. Chatbots, agents, concierge systems, automations. Our people were still messaging each other on Teams.This is not a failure story — it is the starting point of a real transformation.In a 12-minute main stage talk, I will share the journey Impresoft followed to become an AI First, Human-led organization: from a fundamental mistake — giving AI to processes instead of people — to the pivot moment, and finally to concrete results. Not just doing things faster, but doing things we could not do before: an MBO system redesigned and deployed in production in four weeks, sales teams delivering sector analyses that previously required a consultant, developers solving problems that once required a senior architect.The common thread is one: if you stop at automation, you are killing AI. Real AI does not just speed up work — it changes what is possible.Three concrete takeaways to bring home. And an invitation: join the AI Compass Club, Impresoft’s initiative to support Italian SMEs on the same journey — with replicable projects, real skills, and true partnerships.Useful AI is not an idea. It is daily practice. And it is already here.

In 12 minutes on the main stage, I will share the concrete journey we followed to turn intent into results — from increasing internal productivity, to accelerating R&D, to the external services we now deliver to clients.

I won’t talk about utopias: I will present architectural choices, targeted experimentation approaches, and operational integrations that generate measurable value.

The message is simple and provocative: useful AI is not an idea, it’s daily practice. And it is a transformative practice, starting with SMEs.

events.title: Pau Garcia | DOMESTIC DATA STREAMERS

AI in practice, practices for AI
events.description:
“AI doesn’t create value.” “The return on AI initiatives is too low and too slow.” “Italian SMEs are falling behind in AI adoption rankings”… But are these expectations realistic? Have we learned from previous technological revolutions? Is the rapid pace of AI evolution accelerating or slowing large-scale adoption?
Our experience from thousands of projects delivered since AI returned to center stage tells us that companies that have truly put AI into practice are already generating tangible value today—but only when supported by a strong practice of AI, built on elements that go beyond technology and are fully integrated into business strategy.

events.title: Digital autonomy in the age of AI
events.description: The past 30 years have marked an unprecedented historical period in the democratization of information. The emergence and evolution of the web, first, and the arrival of social media later, have enabled anyone with internet access to share their thoughts in their most absolute form of freedom, without the mediation of traditional media. However, what once seemed like the beginning of a golden age now confronts us with a paradox: we find ourselves trapped within frameworks built by a few major global information holders, using the very data that all of us have made freely available online over time. Based on these data, these same actors have created the large models for artificial intelligence that we use every day, both in our personal and professional lives, giving us a second illusion of innovation and freedom, despite clear side effects. The use of external services indeed enables immediate scalability, but it also introduces significant challenges when it comes to sensitive or proprietary data. The continuous transfer of information to third-party environments, technological dependency on the provider, the difficulty of predicting operational costs, energy inefficiency, and compliance implications make these models at least debatable. For Europe, this evolution also takes on a broader strategic dimension. Digital sovereignty is not only about data localization, but about the ability to control critical technologies. Fully relying on non-European infrastructures for information processing means exposing oneself to industrial and geopolitical vulnerabilities. So, let us ask ourselves: are we truly free, sovereign? And, above all, digitally autonomous? How can we reverse this trend over the next 30 years?

events.title: Unsupervised Learning for Discovering Structure in Complex Systems
events.description: How does the human mind make sense of raw information without being taught how to see or hear? In this talk we will explore how to build algorithms that can uncover interpretable structure from large collections of unsupervised data like images and video. First, I will describe how to classify every pixel of a collection of images without any human annotations (Unsupervised semantic segmentation) by distilling self-supervised vision models. Second, we’ll see how this basic idea leads us to a new unifying theory of representation learning, and I will show how 20 different common machine learning methods such as dimensionality reduction, clustering, contrastive learning, and spectral methods emerge from a single unified equation. Finally, we’ll use this unified theory to create algorithms that can decode natural language just by watching unlabeled videos of people talking, without any knowledge of text. This work is the first step in our broader effort to translate animals using large scale, unsupervised, and interpretable learners, and the talk will conclude with some of our most recent efforts to analyze the complex vocalizations of Atlantic spotted dolphins.

events.title: True, plausible-indeed, likely. AI as an opaque, statistically reliable oracle
events.description:
Artificial intelligence does not tell the truth. Not even what is merely plausible, for that matter. It tells what is probable—more precisely, what is statistically least wrong among a billion possible attempts. And yet we treat it like an oracle: instant answers, confident tone, no hesitation.

But beneath the glossy surface of generative and predictive algorithms lies a troubling opacity: no one—not even those who designed them—can truly explain why the AI responded the way it did. Its certainty is only statistical: it works on average, not in the individual case.

This talk dismantles the illusion of the transparent oracle and exposes the radical difference between being true and simply not having been disproven by the distribution curve. Between truth and plausibility, a void opens up—one that AI fills with probabilities trained on past data, often biased, always finite.

The result is a paradox: the more statistically reliable AI becomes, the greater the risk that we mistake the probable for the authentic. A provocation to rethink our relationship with machines that do not know what truth is, yet are remarkably good at pretending they do.

events.title: Sovereignty à la carte: how much freedom do you want over your data?
events.description:
Imagine a scale. At the bottom, your data travels on third-party infrastructure, encrypted with keys that — in theory — only you control. One step above, you truly hold those keys yourself. Higher up, the software processing your data is open, auditable, and modifiable. At the top, the entire platform runs within your perimeter, on hardware you can physically touch.
There is no single model of sovereignty. There are levels. And each level comes with a cost, an advantage, and a promise.
In this workshop, we take a journey through this scale — practical, without dogma. We start with hyperscalers — Google Cloud, Microsoft — and examine what it really means to rely on them while holding the encryption keys: what is protected, what is not, and when it is enough. Then we move up: Customer-Managed Keys, BYOK (Bring Your Own Key), all the way to models where the key never leaves your system.
We then reach hybrid AI platforms, built for example on enterprise Kubernetes stacks, where data never leaves your datacenter but cloud power remains accessible. And finally, we reach the top: fully open-source models deployed in completely controlled environments, where every line of code is inspectable and no vendor can change the rules mid-game.
The question is not “which level is best.” The question is: which level is right for you, today, given your regulatory constraints, your industry, and your risk appetite?
A healthcare organization handling patient data does not have the same needs as a fintech startup in a testing phase. A European public administration under the post-AI Act framework does not think like an e-commerce optimizing product recommendations. Sovereignty is not one-size-fits-all. And that is exactly why we have chosen to build a proposal that spans the entire scale: because we believe our job is not to sell a technology, but to help you understand how much freedom you need — and then give it to you. With hyperscalers when enough, with open source when full control is required. We are not here to tell you that the cloud is the enemy. We are here to tell you that the choice must be yours. Informed. Conscious. Reversible. Because true data sovereignty does not start from the server where the model runs. It starts the moment you realize you have the ability to choose.

events.title: Towards AI that understands the Real World
events.description:
Recent advances in AI have been driven by large-scale generative models with impressive capabilities in language, code, and digital tasks. Yet these systems still have a limited understanding of the physical world, human intentions, and real-world context.
In this talk, Pascale Fung will discuss the next frontier of AI: world models.
World models allow AI systems to learn abstract representations of the world from continuous multimodal data, enabling reasoning, planning, memory, and action beyond next-token prediction. Moving toward real-world AI agents requires modeling not only the physical world, but also the mental world - including intent, attention, goals, and social context.
The future of AI will depend on systems that can understand, adapt, and collaborate in the real world, safely and reliably.

In an era dominated by the race for automation, the real risk is not technological but human: building perfect systems within an imperfect ecosystem. This talk proposes a paradigm shift—automation not as a replacement for human work, but as applied wisdom capable of elevating it. Through the real-world experience of the agents powering the SophIA and ThalIA platforms, the session explores three key pillars: 
• Automation as an ethical choice: designing fair and transparent processes, eliminating hidden biases in data and models. 
• Wisdom in automation: integrating a systemic vision that places the well-being of people and the organization at the center. 
• From productivity to human fulfillment: using AI to free up time and value, giving back to people what makes them unique—intuition, empathy, and judgment. 
The journey culminates in an evolved vision of the enterprise, where HR and Finance converge into a single connected intelligence, and where efficiency is no longer just a KPI, but the result of a harmonious balance between technology and humanity.

events.description:
A keynote on why the next era of AI will not be defined only by better tools, but by more people choosing to act like founders.
For decades, software creation was constrained by access: access to technical skills, teams, capital, and institutional permission. Lovable is changing that. More people can now move from idea to working product faster than ever before. As building becomes easier, founder-like behaviours become more important: ownership, speed, judgement, resilience, and the ability to learn in public.
Aino will argue that the underlying shift is behavioural. The people who stand out in the AI era are those who see a gap, take ownership, learn quickly, build something real, and find the community or market that needs it. Being a founder is becoming a way of operating that can apply far beyond the traditional startup path.

Drawing on her experience building Europe’s startup community at Slush, and now leading special projects, community and growth initiatives at Lovable, Aino will explore what happens when software creation opens up to the 99% in the broadest behavioural sense. More people can now participate in building products, companies, communities and new economic value. But building is only the beginning. The founders who win are the ones who turn access into action, action into momentum, and momentum into impact.
The central question is shifting from whether people can build, to what they choose to take responsibility for next.

events.title: Agents that learn: a soft actor-critic approach
events.description:
At AI Week 2026, we will present an architecture for autonomous, adaptable agentic systems oriented toward continuous learning.
At the core of the solution, reasoning is separated from execution: a first multi-agent system composed of “Actors” and “Critics” collaborates in an adversarial setup to define the action strategy, also leveraging the history of past executions. A second multi-agent system, organized hierarchically, is responsible for execution and real-world implementation through specialized agents and operational functions, known as “Tools”.
The system implements a reinforcement learning paradigm, where evaluating agents compare the generated outcome with user expectations, feeding a global and personalized memory that ensures continuous performance improvement and prevents the repetition of errors.
The infrastructure, which is portable on-premise, guarantees full data sovereignty and security, featuring a modular and LLM-agnostic design that eliminates vendor lock-in risk. Finally, the multi-agent architecture ensures maximum explainability and transparency of decision-making processes, enabling the solution to evolve and scale in close collaboration with end users through co-design.

The session will focus on the results of the research conducted within the European Digital Tech Watch (EDTW) initiative, a think tank of the School of Management at the Polytechnic University of Milan dedicated to analyzing the European digital landscape. Through a cross-disciplinary approach, EDTW aims to understand Europe’s positioning in the global landscape in terms of innovation, competitiveness, and digital sovereignty.
Starting from evidence gathered through research involving more than 1,500 companies across 15 European countries, the session will analyze the state of digital technology adoption within large European organizations, highlighting the continent’s level of readiness in relation to the objectives set by the European Union in the race to develop a European AI ecosystem—considered a key element for maintaining and strengthening competitiveness in a rapidly evolving global context.

events.title: AI, automation and the human factor: how LLMs leverage human behaviour at scale
events.description: The AI revolution is making everything faster: both for cyber-attack actors, who are using it to automate advanced attacks at unprecedented speed, and for cybersecurity professionals, who can leverage the same tools to enhance and accelerate their defensive capabilities. In this session, we will explore which areas require strengthened defenses in anticipation of the growing wave of AI-driven threats, and how these tools can be used strategically to reinforce and consolidate our security systems.

Moving beyond traditional conversational automation, agentic AI can reason, take action across systems, and safely complete customer requests end to end.
The focus is on how this new approach to automation improves efficiency, containment, and service continuity, while remaining flexible and easy to design.

events.title: From Earth Observation to Earth Intelligence: How the ESA Φ-lab helps developing solutions to Give the Planet a Voice
events.description:
Earth Observation data already supports decisions across many industries – often without anyone realizing it. Yet despite its enormous value, this data remains difficult to access, fragmented across platforms, and hard to translate into clear, decision-ready insights.
In this presentation, it will be shown how the ESA Φ-lab, and in particular the InCubed programme, supported two companies, GeoVille and Cortecs, to develop terrAIntel, an AI-powered Earth Intelligence platform designed to bridge this gap. The talk explores how AI can move users from programming languages and complex provider-specific workflows toward natural-language interaction, map-based evidence, statistics, and interpretation.
Rather than being another general-purpose LLM, terrAIntel is positioned as a domain-specialized AI layer that helps turn fragmented Earth Observation data into understandable and actionable Earth intelligence.

events.title: Engineering
AutoCM & Meta-AutoCM: E-Commerce Network Analysis
events.description:
The study analyzes a global e-commerce system using AutoCM and Meta-AutoCM models to go beyond traditional sales statistics.
AutoCM identifies direct associations between variables (markets, products, platforms), while Meta-AutoCM reveals functional similarities and systemic impact.
Results show that geography is the main driver, with markets influencing the system far more than product categories.
It highlights “sentinel” markets that detect early changes and “bridge” countries that signal their spread toward Europe and the US.
The combined approach provides a strategic map for geographic segmentation, early-warning monitoring, and optimization of pricing and sales strategies.

events.description: As Artificial Intelligence becomes ubiquitous, leaders and organisations are no longer constrained by a technology gap, but by an imagination gap. Tools are evolving faster than our ability to rethink how we orient collective action, make decisions, and create value alongside machines. In this talk, Henri Allegra proposes a radical shift in perspective: the real challenge of AI is not adoption, but a transformation in the way we think. He introduces hybrid intelligence as a core leadership capability: the intentional integration of human insight, judgment, and values with machine reasoning. Used this way, AI becomes a metacognitive partner, making leaders aware of how they think, not only of what they decide. Leaders will be challenged to unlearn automation-era reflexes and relearn leadership from scratch in an AI-native world. The promise is a deeper human transformation: expanded imagination, renewed agency, and more responsible, innovative organisations in the age of hybrid intelligence.

events.title: ENGAGE Editore
Lost in Translation? How a translation agency reinvented its future in the age of AI.
events.description:
The talk tells the story of how Intrawelt, a translation agency from the Marche region with 35 years of experience in translation, localization, and interpreting services, responded to the challenge of AI instead of being overwhelmed by it, in collaboration with the SPOCRI Lab of the University of Macerata led by Professor Emanuele Frontoni.

Starting from the catastrophic predictions surrounding the industry, the presentation shows how the global translation market has actually continued to grow (+5.6% annually, from USD 56 billion to a projected USD 124 billion by 2037), while still acknowledging the real impact on professionals in the sector.

Intrawelt’s response was the development of scenia®, a SaaS platform created in collaboration with the University of Macerata and the company Aidapt. The platform integrates translation memories, specialized AI, and human professionals (human-in-the-loop) into a model where costs progressively decrease as validated translation knowledge accumulates.

The core thesis is that translation and AI have become commodities, but the real product has always been — and still is — the expert management of complex linguistic projects.

events.title: The Cloud Above Clouds
events.description:
Cloud strategies have reached their limits. Today, companies simultaneously manage public clouds, on-premise systems, and workloads distributed at the edge, but fragmentation, vendor lock-in, and inconsistent governance models continue to slow down innovation. Elemento Cloud proposes a transformative alternative: a Global Cloud Layer that sits above any infrastructure and unifies them into a single architectural continuum.

This session will show how Elemento’s form-follows-function approach enables organizations to design their workloads first and only then decide where to run them, without constraints and in a fully seamless way. Abstracting cloud providers, consolidating control planes, and making workloads truly portable eliminates the operational silos that the traditional multi-cloud model has never been able to overcome. Participants will see how the Elemento platform redefines the concept of cloud freedom: native integration between private and public environments, deterministic governance and compliance, and the ability to place workloads where performance is optimal, without depending on a single vendor. “The Cloud above Clouds” represents a concrete vision for companies that want to regain technological sovereignty, accelerate digital transformation, and manage their infrastructure according to their own rules — not those of cloud providers.

events.title: Alteus Medical: practical AI support for better clinical consultations

Doctors work under constant pressure: limited time, fragmented patient information, and growing documentation requirements. This often reduces time for what matters most - the patient conversation and clinical decision. Alteus Medical is an AI-powered clinical copilot, part of the alteus.ai platform, designed to support doctors before, during, and after consultations. It helps clinicians quickly understand patient context, ask better follow-up questions, and prepare structured draft documentation for review and approval. In this session, we show how Alteus Medical supports three key outcomes: faster access to relevant patient history and medical context. Better consultation flow through contextual AI assistance. Clearer, more consistent doctor-approved documentation with less administrative effort. The presentation also highlights why governance is essential for healthcare AI adoption: privacy, role-based access, auditability, and human clinical oversight are built into the workflow. The goal is practical impact at scale - helping clinical teams work more efficiently while keeping medical judgment fully in the hands of doctors.

events.title: Private AI and Sovereign Cloud: beyond the myths… in other words, the whole truth that no one has (yet) told you!
events.description: The safe use of Artificial Intelligence has become the mantra of every sales brochure, every institutional strategy plan, and every conference keynote speech—including this one. This session will guide the audience through a three-step journey: what regulations and standards actually say, and where things are really heading (without oversimplification); what is technically possible today (with solutions that can be implemented now, without trade-offs between security, sovereignty, and real cost awareness); and what is still missing culturally, industrially, and politically for Sovereign AI to stop being a slogan and become real infrastructure. events.title: From image to asset: Cognitive Intelligence for encoding visual data

events.title: UNaIVERSE: Autonomous Digital Societies for Humans and Decentralized AI
events.description:
UNaIVERSE is an innovative startup that introduces a transformative approach to the technological stack, moving "above" standard Agentic AI frameworks to create autonomous communities of humans and AIs. By leveraging peer-to-peer (P2P) networks, UNaIVERSE enables private, on-premise implementations of complex industrial processes, bypassing the risks of centralized cloud infrastructures, promoting control and integration with heterogeneous systems, beyond LLM-centric frameworks. While modern web and social AI systems have expanded human capability, they have also compromised privacy, centralized power, and created unsustainable energy demands. UNaIVERSE advocates for a fundamental paradigm shift grounded in privacy preservation, energy efficiency, and distributed design, as championed by Collectionless AI. Key highlights of this speech: (1) The Shift to the Edge: Relocating intelligence from centralized servers to edge devices. This utilizes local computational power while maintaining sophisticated, integrative information sharing and long-term learning. (2) The "Worlds" Concept: A re-organization of the Web into autonomous ecosystems. These "Worlds" function as digital societies where agents learn, reason, and plan based on collective constraints and shared intents. (3) Decentralized Protocols: Utilizing P2P communication to ensure that individual and collective goals are met without intermediary surveillance.
We will demonstrate how UNaIVERSE instantiates this vision, providing a platform where decentralized AI and human-AI coexistence are governed by privacy-first principles.

events.title: Agent Sovereignty
events.description:
Italian companies are deploying AI agents without knowing where they are going, what they are saying, or what is leaving their perimeter. This is not a technological problem, but a legal and strategic exposure that is already in effect: Mind Breach, AI Act, GDPR, ISO 42001. It will not disappear with the next model.
In this speech, the CEO and CTO of Pupau.ai explain what it means to govern an agentic company today: the difference between deploying agents in production and keeping them under control, and why companies that have already made this leap are turning governance into a hard-to-copy competitive advantage.
The thesis: the 2027 agentic enterprise will not be defined by how many agents it has in production, but by its ability to govern them. Those who build today the cognitive infrastructure with data sovereignty, native auditability, and controlled deployment (on-premise or private cloud) are not just reducing risk. They are building the key differentiator of the next industrial cycle.
With real production use cases: public institutions, industry, large-scale retail (GDO), and professional services.

events.title: From dynamo to co-thinker: why your AI isn’t working yet
events.description:
When factories first gained access to electricity, for decades they simply replaced the steam engine with a dynamo—same factory, same layouts, same belts. Productivity didn’t move. The real leap came only when a new generation of entrepreneurs had the courage to tear down the factory and rebuild it from scratch around the electric motor.
Today, with artificial intelligence, we are in the dynamo phase. Companies buy copilots and layer them onto unchanged processes: AI summarizes, generates drafts, answers questions. Useful—but it’s not transformation, it’s cosmetic automation. The real discontinuity has a name: moving from co-pilot to co-thinker. Not a faster assistant, but a system that enters the decision-making process, understands context, reasons about implications, and raises risks no one in the room is considering.
This will be illustrated through a case every company knows: a strategic procurement. A multi-million contract, eleven months of negotiation, thirty people at the table—and a liability clause hidden on page 47 that none of the thirty noticed. The co-thinker did. We will see how, concretely: specialized agents, structured organizational memory, and a workflow where AI doesn’t assist the team but thinks alongside the team. Those leaving this talk will have a framework to understand whether their company is using AI like a dynamo—and what it takes to rebuild the factory.

events.title: Your AI passed the test. Now what?
events.description: AI is moving beyond static models and one-off evaluations into systems that continuously adapt, learn, and operate autonomously, often inside real environments, not just test datasets. Most teams still rely on benchmark-driven evaluation, which is useful, but increasingly misleading. It tells you how a model performs at a single point in time, not how it behaves once it’s deployed and interacting in real environments. And that’s the problem: the environment itself changes, adapts, and evolves, so AI must operate in a world that never stands still.

events.title: When physical space becomes intelligent
events.description:
For years, we have made the digital world intelligent. Every click, every interaction, every online behavior has become measurable, analyzable, and predictable.
But as soon as we step outside the digital realm, we still enter a nearly blind world. Retail stores, restaurants, commercial spaces, and physical environments—where most real economic activity happens—continue to make decisions based on intuition, experience, and incomplete data.
This talk explores what happens when the physical world finally becomes intelligent.
Through Edge AI, behavioral analytics, and real-time data, physical spaces can now understand flows, behaviors, conversions, and operational dynamics that were previously invisible—transforming simple environments into systems capable of observing, understanding, and reacting.
This is not a future vision. It is already happening. And it will change the way we design, manage, and experience real-world spaces.

events.description: This talk explores how to leverage competitive environments to generate meaningful insights into assessing and benchmarking both individuals and organizations. What began as a way to evaluate technical skill has evolved into a framework for understanding performance under pressure, adaptability, and real-world problem solving. As AI becomes embedded in workflows, capability is no longer measured in isolation but through how professionals operate alongside AI to enhance speed, accuracy, and decision making, and increasingly through scenarios where autonomous agents operate and compete independently. Drawing on insights from large-scale AI vs human competitions and ongoing cybersecurity events, this session highlights key signals of this shift and offers a forward-looking view on how AI is reshaping the cybersecurity talent landscape and how assessment will evolve in the near future.

In this talk, we'll explain why "liquid teams"—combining internal talent, verified freelance specialists, and AI agents—are becoming the new operating model for innovation.
We'll share the solution Shakers has implemented to drive this change: an AI-powered matching and delivery process that reduces the time to find the first ideal candidate to between 24 and 48 hours and compresses the onboarding process from weeks to days, improving both speed and quality. It starts with building an avatar, choosing distinctive physical features such as eye and hair color, body proportions, and outfit, and placing our influencer directly into a scene. Not a generic element, but something contextualized and recognizable.
The avatar then comes to life through animation, transforming what was just a static image a moment earlier into a video.
The end result is a real product sponsorship video, entirely filmed with the character we created. A format that brands and creators use every day—and that is now within everyone’s reach.

The talk presents a consulting approach that starts from a strategic audit to design AI-ready marketing and communication ecosystems, where data, content, and touchpoints become truly queryable. It manages automated multichannel interaction and support; transforms documents and procedures into a queryable, generative knowledge base; collects and organizes real-time operational data in the cloud for end-to-end process management; and converts this data into KPIs and strategic insights to support decision-making and compliance. events.title: The carbon ROI of AI. How much does Artificial Intelligence cost in CO2? What benefits does it generate instead? The first quantitative study on Italian SMEs.
events.description: Generative AI is presented as an ally of the transition: it optimizes consumption, predicts waste, and accelerates ESG reporting. But every query to a language model consumes energy. Global data centers could double their electricity consumption by 2030, with an estimated carbon footprint of between 32 and 80 million tons of CO₂ in 2025 alone. Around 60% of the new electricity demand from data centers will be covered by fossil fuels. No one has ever measured this paradox at the level of individual Italian companies. This white paper does so for the first time: through an analysis of companies and sectors, it assesses the net carbon impact of AI adoption—comparing the emissions generated by the use of AI tools (infrastructure, computing, cloud) with the emissions saved thanks to the efficiency gains enabled by AI itself (logistics, energy, processes). The result is a “carbon balance sheet of AI” by company type, size, and sector, accompanied by future scenarios.

events.title: Reducing invisible costs and operational risk: a real-world case of AI in enterprise systems integration
events.description: Manual files, offline reconciliations, and non-integrated systems generate a significant hidden cost: time, inefficiencies, and the risk of errors in core processes. In this talk, we will present a real-world case in which an AI-supported middleware architecture made it possible to eliminate manual activities, standardize information flows, and create a single control point for enterprise data. The focus is not on AI as a technology, but on its tangible impact: reduced operational time, greater data reliability, and stronger governance. This session is designed for CIOs and CFOs who want to turn IT complexity into a competitive advantage without introducing further fragmentation.

events.title: NeuroForge
events.description:
What if training were no longer designed, but generated?
In a context where skills become obsolete increasingly quickly, traditional training models are no longer sufficient. NeuroForge introduces a new paradigm: a system in which artificial intelligence does not merely support learning, but builds it, adapts it, and evolves it in real time. Starting from existing knowledge, a network of AI agents transforms static materials into dynamic learning experiences, generating multimodal content and structured learning paths in moments. But the real shift happens during learning itself: users interact with an intelligent system that understands context, responds in a targeted way, and guides the exploration of information. Training thus becomes a living experience. Thanks to an adaptive gamification engine, every piece of content becomes an interactive environment that evolves based on the learner’s actions, mistakes, and progress. The AI observes, learns, and continuously modifies the path, making it increasingly personalized, effective, and relevant. It is no longer the user who adapts to the course.
It is the course that adapts to the user. NeuroForge redefines the very concept of learning: from a static process to an intelligent, continuous, and generative system.

MAITIME was created to give that time back. events.title: AI: oasis or mirage?
events.description:
We live in an era in which artificial intelligence always seems to have an answer. It writes, analyzes, and suggests. But what happens when a technology that appears perfectly credible is not seeking truth, but probability?

Starting from the powerful metaphor of an oasis in the desert, this talk guides the audience through one of the most urgent themes in contemporary innovation: the risk of entrusting operational and strategic decisions to AI systems designed to be persuasive before they are reliable. This is not a technical talk about artificial intelligence, but a reflection on the future of work, leadership, and business decision-making. From blind trust in chatbots to the evolution toward intelligent agents capable of supporting real operational choices, the talk explores the transition from the era of artificial intelligence to that of augmented intelligence. A keynote that blends vision, storytelling, and real-world examples to address the crucial question of the coming years: not how much AI we will use, but which AI we can truly trust.

However, the real differentiator is not simply having data, but having high-quality data: accurate, complete, integrated with company data, and continuously updated. This quality is a prerequisite for effective decision-making and for leveraging AI, which acts as a multiplier: it creates value when built on solid data, but amplifies errors when the foundations are weak. Data and insights, embedded within automated processes, thus become part of a continuous cycle of learning and improvement that ensures scalable value.

events.title: Approved, developed, wrong. The invisible cost that AI is multiplying
events.description:
Every digital project has a moment when its fate is decided. It is usually not when the software goes into production. It happens much earlier — in a meeting where everyone nods, but no one has truly seen.

Unvalidated flows, ignored exceptions, expectations that seem shared but are not: these are not technical problems. They are decisions made in the dark. And the bill comes later, in the form of rework, delays, and budgets that never add up.

Today, AI introduces a variable that changes everything: it can compress development times, automate processes, and multiply execution speed. But if the project starts off wrong, AI does not fix it — it accelerates it. It automates ambiguity. It scales error. It makes a merely plausible project more expensive, and faster. Anyone developing software sees it every day: the problem almost never starts in the code. It starts in the moment when someone said “we understand each other” and it wasn’t true. This talk explores that moment: where digital initiative risk truly originates, why managers approve with less information than they believe, and what mindset shift is needed to see before deciding — not to build more, but to get things wrong much less.

The adopted solution, Catenary, an AI system designed for regulated environments, has revolutionized this approach: it understands regulatory and corporate documents, automatically connects them, makes the entire corpus queryable in natural language, and provides contextualized, accurate, and traceable answers without replacing decision-making responsibilities.
The results? Intelligent support for compliance and day-to-day operations, promoting sustainability by reducing complexity, errors, and dependence on specialized expertise, embodying a model of ethical and sustainable AI for the circular economy.

events.title: From clustering to action: how agentic AI transforms retail from reactive to autonomous
events.description: Every retailer knows the pain of margins eroded by promotions and of customer loyalty that never quite takes off. Starting from a real case of a fashion e-commerce, we will show how AI-driven customer segmentation based on clustering is already capable today of mapping precise behavioral patterns, from high-spending customers to “opportunity seekers.” But the real revolution begins when AI stops observing and starts deciding. We will explore the evolution toward Agentic AI, capable of making the entire marketing and CRM cycle autonomous: agents that update clusters in real time, generate hyper-personalized communications, and orchestrate recovery campaigns to intercept at-risk customers before it is too late. We will conclude with a necessary reflection on governance and the AI Act: your CRM knows who your customers are, but does your AI already know what to do—and when to do it autonomously? A talk designed for C-level executives who want to see how AI can move from data to action, in compliance with the AI Act and algorithmic accountability.

events.title: The Brand in the Age of Artificial Intelligence
events.description: Artificial intelligence is reshaping the way brands are perceived, positioned, and communicated—often without companies even being aware of it. Together with EY Studio+, we will address key topics for brand growth in the age of artificial intelligence: authenticity as the only defense against algorithmic commoditization; human advantage as a source of competitive edge—where the more machines advance, the more the human element matters; monitoring and influencing positioning, and how to govern one’s narrative; and AI product design, focusing on how to build AI products that convey brand authenticity.

events.title: Beyond Deployment: how to evaluate and manage the reliability of LLMs over time
events.description: The large-scale adoption of generative models requires new forms of governance and control. We will explore how organizations can continuously evaluate the quality of responses, the consistency of behaviors, and the robustness of LLM outputs over time, through practical approaches and real-world examples. We will also discuss several emerging methods for measuring and managing model reliability, highlighting their strategic implications for business.

events.description: The adoption of AI in organizations is accelerating, but often in a fragmented way: isolated projects, unmanaged risks, and value that is difficult to measure. The AI Control Tower transforms AI from ad hoc experimentation into a systemic lever, structured around four pillars: Security, Compliance, Value, and Strategic Alignment. An operational workshop for those who want not just to “do AI,” but to govern it.

events.title: How AI is reshaping the customer approach in claims management processes
events.description:
Claims management involves high volumes, operational complexity, and strong pressure on time, cost, and service quality. Today, AI and Generative AI are transforming this field by enabling new interaction models across the entire claims lifecycle.
Advanced virtual assistants make it possible to automate key processes, improving the customer experience by removing time constraints and reducing waiting times. The talk will present the benefits of adoption from both the customer’s perspective and the insurance company’s point of view.

events.title: AI as a decision-making infrastructure: what changes for business decision-makers
events.description: Artificial intelligence is no longer just an operational support, but an infrastructure that structures, guides, and often anticipates decisions within organizations. This talk explores how AI is redefining roles, responsibilities, and decision-making processes at the managerial level. At the core is not only performance, but also risk governance, the quality of decisions, and their traceability. This leads to new needs: adaptive control models, integration between compliance and business, and a real capacity for human oversight. For decision-makers, the challenge is not simply to use AI, but to govern it without delegating decision-making power to it.

events.title: Re-invent CRM: Prioritize Customers, Simplify Processes
From Hype to Operational Reality: building the Foundations of AI
events.description: AI is evolving faster than companies’ ability to adopt it. This talk explores the relationship between AI and humanity, the main friction points in adoption, and the gap between announcements and real integration, showing how infrastructure and architectures are now the true key to scaling AI.

events.title: Arsenalia, Electrolux Professional Group & Microsoft: Governing Augmented Intelligence. Electrolux Professional Group’s journey through governance, training, and organizational change.
events.description:
AI does not simply add new tools: it redistributes intelligence. When this capability becomes accessible, widespread, and operational within workflows, the focus is no longer the technology itself, but the organization’s ability to govern it. This is what we define as augmented intelligence: a condition in which people, processes, and decisions extend their potential through distributed capabilities integrated into everyday work.
Electrolux Group presents a concrete case in which governance, internal training, and guided adoption become strategic levers to transform experimentation and curiosity into a real, coherent, and sustainable organizational capability. This is not a theoretical discussion about AI, but a practical perspective on how to make it operational, governed, and relevant in daily activities. Because the challenge is not bringing AI into the company, but enabling the organization to evolve with it.

events.title: Arsenalia and the Municipality of Milan: practical AI in service of citizens
events.description: From the digital agent for registry and tax services to AI-based monitoring of building permits, from automatic anonymization in images related to penalties to NLP support for the 020202 contact center, up to the Extended Digital Twin for urban governance: the Municipality of Milan already has AI embedded in its processes. As the first Italian public administration with an AI Manifesto, Milan is the smartest city in Italy. Luca Curioni speaks with Antonio Zimmitti of Arsenalia about how an administration with 526 services and 3 million users per day is innovating in a concrete, ethical, and scalable way.

events.title: Can AI hack? Benchmarking frontier models against real-world web vulnerabilities
events.description: This is a technically-informed talk focused on measuring the built-in offensive security capabilities of frontier LLMs. Rather than relying on vendor claims or synthetic evaluations, we designed a rigorous, reproducible benchmark: 10 models tested against real Hack The Box challenges spanning the OWASP Top 10, with 10 independent runs per challenge and identical conditions across the board. The talk covers the methodology behind this design, walks through the results — including where models succeed and where they fail.

events.title: The Memory Wall: Why AI Agents Fail (and How to Fix Them)
events.description: Today's AI agents run on duct tape: separate systems for transactions, analytics, and vectors, stitched together with brittle ETL pipelines and growing engineering overhead. That approach won't survive the next wave of agentic AI, where enterprises need to support millions of concurrent agents, each with persistent memory, real-time data access, and consistent state. This session introduces the architecture that supports millions of agents: a converged distributed SQL platform that unifies OLTP, real-time analytics, and native vector search in a single ACID-compliant system, handling relational, vector, and full-text demands in one query layer. We'll walk through the Decide-Validate-Remember loop that production teams use to reduce token costs through persistent context and scale multi-agent workflows without state drift.

events.title: The thinking territory: how AI and IoT transform distributed data into intelligent decisions
events.description:
A city produces millions of signals every day: traffic, mobility, environment, consumption, events, and people flows. For years, we have collected this data without truly managing to turn it into decision-making capability. Today, Artificial Intelligence is changing the paradigm: no longer passive dashboards, but territorial systems capable of interpreting context, anticipating phenomena, and suggesting operational actions.
In this workshop, we will explore how the integration of AI, IoT, and Smart Land platforms is redefining territorial governance. From urban mobility management to hydrogeological risk prevention, from predictive analysis of tourist flows to environmental monitoring, we will see how data coming from sensors, mobile networks, infrastructure, and public sources can converge into an intelligent and interoperable ecosystem.
Through real-world cases and live demos, we will show how the territorial Digital Twin evolves from a simple representation of the city into a true cognitive decision-support system.
Because the future of Smart Lands is not about having more data. It is about having territories capable of understanding it.

events.title: Practical Approaches to Generative AI Amongst the World's top News Publishers
events.description: News organisations around the world are rapidly integrating generative AI into their workflows, moving from experimentation to practical implementation. This session explores how leading publishers are using AI across the newsroom—from newsgathering and research to content creation, packaging, and distribution. Drawing on real-world case studies, it will highlight the tools, processes, and organisational approaches that are delivering value today. The talk will also examine the challenges of scaling AI responsibly, balancing efficiency with editorial integrity, and identifying where human expertise remains essential.
